_comment: Wording for the live vision test: the Vision Assessment (/assessment/) and the Screen Settings Check (/screen-check/). Draft for Lions Services to approve (Dana). The assistant may voice only the lines under 'say' with the natural voice. Scoring rules live in server/lib/screen-check.mjs, not here. No client data ever goes in this file.

say.intro: Hi, I'm the Vision 360 screen check. In about ten minutes, we'll find the text size, colors, speaking speed and pointer that are easiest for you, and set them up as we go. Press the Space bar, or say ready, to begin.
say.assessIntro: Hi, I'm the Vision 360 vision assessment. In about ten minutes, I'll ask you to read some short phrases, name some pictures, and pick the colors and pointer that are easiest for you to see. I'll set them up on this page as we go. Press the Space bar, or say ready, to begin.
say.screenReader: Okay. I'll stay quiet so your screen reader can lead. Everything on this page works with the keyboard.
say.practice: First, a quick practice. You can answer by talking, by pressing a button, or by typing. Say ready, or press the Space bar.
say.deviceFix: Thanks. Which are you using: a phone, a tablet, or a computer?
say.goal: What would you like to do on this device? For example, read email, video call family, or read the news. You can also say skip.
say.rateIntro: Let's set how fast I talk. This is my slowest speed. Say faster, slower, or keep this.
say.rateNow: This is how I sound now. Faster, slower, or keep this?
say.magIntro: Now the text size. I'll show a word. Say the word, type it, or say I can't tell. There are no wrong answers.
say.magDone: Thank you. I've set the text to a size that should be comfortable.
say.readIntro: Now some reading. I'll show a short phrase. Read it out loud, or type it. If you can't read it, say I can't tell. There are no wrong answers.
say.picIntro: Now some pictures. I'll show a house, an apple, a circle or a square. Say which one you see, or press its button. If you can't tell, say I can't tell.
say.picDone: Thank you. That tells us how big pictures and icons need to be for you.
say.contrastIntro: Now colors. I'll show two choices, one on the left and one on the right. Say left or right for the one that's easier to read, or say same.
say.contrastNext: Which is easier to read: left or right?
say.contrastDone: Thanks. I've switched to those colors.
say.cursorIntro: Now the mouse pointer. When you find the pointer, click the big round button. If you can't find it, say I can't find it, or press the N key.
say.cursorNext: Find the pointer, then click the round button.
say.cursorColor: Which pointer is easier to see: left or right?
say.boldIntro: One more. Which text is easier to read: left or right?
say.boldDone: Thanks. I've set the text weight.
say.review: All done. I've set your text size, colors, speaking speed and pointer. Say keep, or press the Space bar, to keep them.
say.contactAsk: Would you like someone from Lions Services to contact you about these settings? Say yes or no.
say.finished: Thank you. Your results are on the screen. You can print them, or save them as a P D F.
say.cantHear: Sorry, I didn't catch that. You can also press a button.
say.stopped: Okay, I've stopped listening. Press the Space bar when you want me to listen again.
say.deviceAsk: You're using {device}. Is that right? Say yes or no.
say.guideIntro: Here's how to set this up on your own device. I'll read one step at a time. Say next, or press the Space bar, for the next step.

guides._comment: Read-aloud setup steps for the person's own device, by system and setting. Draft: check each path on a current device before Lions Services signs off (menus move between system versions).

ios.name: iPhone or iPad
textSize: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Display and Text Size.
Turn on Larger Accessibility Sizes, then drag the slider to the right until the text is comfortable.
zoom: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Zoom, and turn Zoom on.
To zoom in or out, double-tap the screen with three fingers.
contrast: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Display and Text Size, and turn on Increase Contrast.
For light text on a dark background, open Settings, then Display and Brightness, and choose Dark.
bold: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Display and Text Size, and turn on Bold Text.
speech: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Spoken Content.
Turn on Speak Selection or Speak Screen, then move the Speaking Rate slider.

android.name: Android phone or tablet
textSize: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Display size and text. On a Samsung, it's Settings, then Accessibility, then Vision enhancements.
Drag the Font size slider, and the Display size slider, until the text is comfortable.
zoom: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Magnification, and turn on the Magnification shortcut.
Use the shortcut, then pinch with two fingers to zoom.
contrast: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Display size and text, and turn on High contrast text.
For light text on a dark background, open Settings, then Display, and turn on Dark theme.
bold: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Display size and text, and turn on Bold text.
speech: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Text-to-speech output.
Move the Speech rate slider, then tap Play to hear it.

mac.name: Mac
textSize: Open the Apple menu, then System Settings, then Accessibility, then Display.
Next to Text size, choose a larger size. To make everything bigger, open System Settings, then Displays, and choose Larger Text.
zoom: Open System Settings, then Accessibility, then Zoom, and turn on Use keyboard shortcuts to zoom.
Press Option, Command and the equals sign to zoom in.
contrast: Open System Settings, then Accessibility, then Display, and turn on Increase contrast.
For light text on a dark background, open System Settings, then Appearance, and choose Dark.
bold: The Mac has no setting for bold text everywhere. A larger text size usually helps more.
speech: Open System Settings, then Accessibility, then Spoken Content.
Move the Speaking rate slider, then press Play to hear it.
pointer: Open System Settings, then Accessibility, then Display, then Pointer.
Drag the Pointer size slider. You can also change the pointer's outline and fill color there.

windows.name: Windows computer
textSize: Open Start, then Settings, then Accessibility, then Text size.
Drag the slider until the sample text is comfortable, then select Apply.
zoom: Press the Windows key and the plus sign together to open Magnifier.
Press the Windows key and plus or minus to zoom in or out. Press the Windows key and Escape to close it.
contrast: Open Start, then Settings, then Accessibility, then Contrast themes.
Choose a theme such as Night sky, then select Apply.
bold: Windows has no setting for bold text everywhere. A larger text size usually helps more.
speech: Open Start, then Settings, then Accessibility, then Narrator.
Under Narrator's voice, move the Speed slider.
pointer: Open Start, then Settings, then Accessibility, then Mouse pointer and touch.
Choose a pointer style, such as white, black or a custom color like yellow, and drag the Size slider.

chromeos.name: Chromebook
textSize: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Display and magnification.
Change the display size. In the Chrome browser, you can also open Settings, then Appearance, and choose a larger Font size.
zoom: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Display and magnification, and turn on Fullscreen magnifier.
contrast: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Display and magnification, and turn on Color inversion.
For a dark look, open Settings, then Personalization, and choose Dark.
bold: Chromebooks have no setting for bold text everywhere. A larger display size usually helps more.
speech: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Text-to-speech, then Text-to-speech voice settings.
pointer: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Cursor and touchpad.
Turn on Show large mouse cursor, drag the size slider, and choose a cursor color.

suggest._comment: Why each kind of service is suggested on the results page. The organizations themselves come from site/data/organizations.json.
suggest.low_vision_clinic: A low vision clinic can check how you see now and find magnifiers and other aids, because you needed very large text.
suggest.assistive_technology: For help setting these up on your own phone, tablet or computer, and learning to use them.
